skill.name: validate-requirements
skill.description: Validate whether a user request has enough detail, clarity, and context before a quality pipeline continues.
skill.summary: Checks project requirements against saved standards before work begins.
skill.author: AbeJitsu

content.value_statement: Vague requests slow quality pipelines and cause rework. This skill checks requirements against project standards before the next step.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a request has enough detail to start work.
Compares input against saved validation rules for the project type.
Identifies missing clarity, context, format, or constraints.
Returns specific issues and a recommendation to proceed or clarify.
Suggests focused clarification questions when requirements are incomplete.
limitations: It depends on saved project standards when custom standards are expected.
It does not create the requested feature or document after validation.
It cannot verify external links or private context unless provided by the user.
It may need user judgment for subjective completeness standards.

use_cases.title: Screen feature requests
use_cases.description: Check whether a feature request includes purpose, constraints, behavior, and success criteria before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review engineering prompts
use_cases.description: Validate that coding requests include enough technical context, examples, and expected outcomes.

use_cases.title: Gate content briefs
use_cases.description: Confirm that writing tasks include topic, audience, format, and key requirements before drafting begins.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a simple request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use validate-requirements on this request: [paste request]. Tell me if it is ready or what is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Check against project standards
prompt_templates.scenario: Use saved standards for a known project type.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this request for a [project type] project. Compare it with the saved standards and list missing requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare clarification questions
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn incomplete input into focused next questions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this incomplete request and ask only the most important clarification questions needed before work starts.

prompt_templates.title: Run a pipeline readiness gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced validation before design, coding, or writing work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as the first quality gate. Validate the requirements, classify each issue, and recommend whether the pipeline should proceed.

output_examples.output: Invalid. The request needs purpose, expected behavior, props, accessibility needs, and selection rules before implementation can begin.

output_examples.input: Create a searchable team member dropdown with keyboard navigation, options, onSelect, and placeholder props.
output_examples.output: Valid. The request includes component purpose, behavior, key interactions, and required interface details.

output_examples.input: Write a blog post about onboarding new developers.
output_examples.output: Needs clarification. Ask for target audience, post length, tone, main points, and publication format.

best_practices: Run this skill before design, coding, writing, or refactoring work begins.
Keep project standards current so validation matches the team process.
Ask only focused clarification questions when the request is close to ready.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as a substitute for product or engineering judgment.
Do not reject a request when one or two targeted questions would unblock it.
Do not treat generic standards as complete when project-specific rules exist.

faq.question: What does this skill validate?
faq.answer: It validates clarity, completeness, context, format, and alignment with saved project standards.

faq.question: Does it write the final output?
faq.answer: No. It decides whether the input is ready for the next step in the workflow.

faq.question: Can it work without custom standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use general validation rules when no saved standards are available.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Teams can use it before implementation, content creation, design work, or refactoring tasks.

faq.question: What happens when requirements are incomplete?
faq.answer: It lists specific missing information and recommends focused clarification before continuing.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
